sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1.
3. Respondent No.2 who is served in the matter has remained unrepresented before this Court.
4.

FIR in Crime No.132/2024 was registered by Bidadi Police Station, Ramanagara District against the petitioner herein initially for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC, on the basis of first information dated 06.04.2024 received from respondent No.2 herein who is the father of the victim NC: 2024:KHC:37493 girl, aged about 16 years 9 months as on the said date.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner and the victim girl were traced together and brought back to their village.
The victim girl was subjected to medical examination and her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, was also recorded.
The petitioner was arrested and produced before the jurisdictional Court on 14.04.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.

Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
5.
The bail application filed by the petitioner before the Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.384/2024 was dismissed on 12.06.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is an youngster, aged about 25 years having no criminal antecedents.
He submits that the petitioner and the victim girl are in love and the victim girl had voluntarily accompanied the petitioner to his mother's house at Malur.

Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
7.
Per contra, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 has opposed the petition.
He submits that as on the date of incident NC: 2024:KHC:37493 the victim girl was a minor.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.
8. The material on record would go to show that the first informant had approached the Bidadi Police Station on 06.04.2024 after his minor daughter who had gone to her school had not returned home.

It is averred in the first information that the first informant was informed that, the victim girl was seen riding pillion along with the petitioner and therefore FIR in Crime No.132/2024 was registered against the petitioner.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner and the victim girl were traced together and brought to their village.

The petitioner was produced before the jurisdictional Court and remanded to judicial custody on 14.04.2024.
9.
The victim girl was subjected to medical examination and before the doctor she has stated that she was in love with the petitioner and had voluntarily gone along with him.

In her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, before the learned Magistrate the victim girl has stated that she was in love with the petitioner and on 06.04.2024 she had voluntarily gone along with the petitioner to Malur and stayed in the house of the petitioner's mother for 7 days and during NC:
2024:KHC:37493 the said period she had sex with the petitioner.
The victim girl has stated that her parents came to Malur and brought the petitioner and her back to their village.
The petitioner is an youngster having no criminal antecedents.
The allegations found in the charge sheet are required to be proved in a full- fledged trial.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.

10. Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail is required to be answered affirmatively.
11.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail in Spl.C.C.No.95/2024 pending before the Court of I Addl. District & Sessions Judge-FTSC-1, Ramanagara, arising out of Crime No.132/2024 registered by Bidadi Police Station, Ramanagara District for the offences punishable under Sections 363 & 376 of IPC, Section 4, 5(L) & 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, subject to the following conditions:
